entities.summary: Marcos Cesar Pontes is a Brazilian Air Force pilot, engineer, AEB astronaut, politician and author. He became the first South American and the first Lusophone to go into space when he docked onto the International Space Station aboard Soyuz TMA-8 on 30 March 2006. He is the only Brazilian to have completed the NASA astronaut training program, although he switched to training in Russia after NASA's Space Shuttle program encountered problems. After Jair Bolsonaro's election as President of Brazil in 2018, Pontes was officially nominated to be Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation, a post which he accepted days later and assumed when Bolsonaro's government began.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the first South American and Lusophone to go into space, Marcos Pontes's historic mission in 2006 marked a significant milestone for Brazil's space program and paved the way for increased international cooperation. His selection as Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation under Jair Bolsonaro's government further underscored his impact on Brazilian politics.
